question_stem:
A binary star consists of two stars A and B that orbit one another, as illustrated in Fig. 1.1.
The stars are in circular orbits with the centres of both orbits at point P, a distance d from the centre of star A.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain why the centripetal force acting on both stars has the same magnitude.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The period of the orbit of the stars about point P is $4.0\,\text{years}$.
Calculate the angular speed $\omega$ of the stars.
$$\omega = \dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\,\text{rad}\,\text{s}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use your answers in (a)(ii) and (b)(i) to determine the mass $M_\text{B}$ of star B.
Explain your working.
$$M_\text{B} = \dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\,\text{kg}$$
